title: Reservoir head-sampling + tag suppression to cut tracing hot-path CPU and latency
creator: Maya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce CPU and latency overhead from distributed tracing on high-QPS endpoints while preserving tail-event fidelity for debugging. Current tracing adds ~1.8-2.4ms median overhead and up to 6-8ms for some services at peak QPS due to allocations and tag/attribute serialization on every request. Success criteria: reduce median tracing overhead to <0.5ms on sampled-negative paths, maintain 99th-percentile error capture unchanged, and drop end-to-end CPU spent on trace hot-path by >=50% in staging load tests.

Design summary: implement a reservoir-based head sampler (lightweight O(1) decision) evaluated at ingress that: 1) makes a fast deterministic sample decision using a per-endpoint reservoir window to ensure representative samples across bursty traffic; 2) short-circuits the runtime by skipping span object allocation and attribute tokenization on non-sampled requests (fast no-op path); 3) suppresses and coalesces low-cardinality tags (e.g., feature flags, internal request metadata) on the hot-path and emits them only when a full-sample is taken; 4) retains a small edge-case buffer (ring buffer) of recent head-requests to retroactively promote a span to full payload if post-hoc tail-sampling triggers on error conditions.

Technical trade-offs: reservoir windows slightly increase variance vs purely random sampling but improve coverage during bursts. Suppressing tags reduces immediate fidelity; mitigation is twofold: (a) keep a hashed minimal token for every request to allow lightweight grouping in dashboards; (b) automatically enable full capture on error thresholds or when PID-level debugging is enabled.

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind `reservoir_head_sampler` per service. Canary rollout to three low-risk services (auth-proxy, attachments-api, reranker) with a 10% traffic fraction and synthetic load tests. Monitoring: new Grafana panel for sample decision latency, allocation rate, span serialize time, and the retro-promotion ratio. Canary SLOs: no more than 0.2% increase in median API latency and <1% drop in successful error triage leads.

Observability changes: add metrics `trace.sample_decision_latency_ms`, `trace.hotpath_allocs_per_1k_requests`, `trace.tag_suppressed_count`, `trace.retro_promotion_rate`. Add logs on retro-promotion events to a low-QPS debug stream. Update tracing docs and runbook in Confluence.

Testing: microbench harness (go) for fast-path vs slow-path, end-to-end staging test with k6 to validate p50/p95 overhead and CPU impact, unit tests for deterministic reservoir behavior, fuzz tests for ring buffer promotion logic.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Maya Kapoor: Spike complete. Implemented PoC of reservoir decision in ingress proxy. Observed drop of ~65% allocations in the fast-path in microbench (allocs/request from 420 -> 145) but tail error promotion path needs safety bounds to avoid memory spike.

2026-02-25 - Oliver Reed: Design review notes: prefer a pre-allocated small span header object reused on hot-path rather than allocating and discarding; ensure no locks on the fast-path (use atomic counters). Also requested an explicit canary rollback plan tied to canary metric thresholds.

2026-03-01 - SRE (Liu Zhang): Load test results from staging attached (k6 run). Median overhead down to 0.42ms on service A, p99 unchanged for error capture. Observed retro-promotion ratio ~0.8% which is within expected limits. CPU reduced ~48% on the ingress pod group.

2026-03-04 - QA (Kenji Ito): Found an edge case where retro-promotion on batched requests caused duplicated attributes when multiple promotions happened in the same window. Added a mutex-less idempotency check in PoC to fix; needs more fuzz tests.

2026-03-08 - PM (Sofia Chen): Approving canary rollout. Requested a short doc in Confluence explaining when to disable tag suppression for customer-facing investigations. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Reservoir+Head+Sampler

2026-03-10 - Oliver Reed: Opened PR for ingress-proxy implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421. Notes in PR: uses lock-free ring buffer for promotion candidates, reuses pre-allocated span header to avoid GC churn, and emits suppressed-tag metrics. Requesting reviews from @liuzhang and @kenji-qa.
next_steps: Finish PR reviews and merge behind feature flag, instrument canary services, run 48h canary with synthetic load, iterate on suppression rules based on retro-promotion telemetry, prepare rollout playbook and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Fast-path median tracing overhead <0.5ms on canary services under synthetic load. 2) Hot-path allocations reduced >=50% vs baseline. 3) Retro-promotion ratio <2% with no memory regressions. 4) No more than 0.2% regression in request success/error triage ability according to debug-sample checks. 5) Documentation & runbook updated.
